summary.text: A 33-year-old woman was referred with three weeks of pyrexia of unknown origin and pancytopenia (WBC 3.2 k/μl, hemoglobin 7.8 g/dl, platelets 25,000/μl) and, once admitted, reported bone aches of the lower back and pelvis, vomiting and diarrhea. Examination showed no organomegaly or lymphadenopathy.

Workup showed markedly raised ferritin and LDH, negative autoimmune, viral and infectious serologies, unremarkable chest radiograph and abdominal sonography, and CEA 17 ng/ml. Bone marrow aspirate showed hypocellular marrow infiltrated by non-hematopoietic cells, and bone marrow pathology showed malignant epithelial infiltration positive for pan CK, CK20 and CDX2, supporting gastrointestinal origin.

CT and MRI showed a malignant rectosigmoid infiltrative lesion, bilateral ovarian masses mostly Krukenberg tumor and bony deposits of the iliac bones and sacrum; colonoscopy found a stenosing rectosigmoid growth whose biopsy matched the bone marrow morphology, giving metastatic rectosigmoid carcinoma.
She was admitted to the isolation ward and started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, and died of sepsis one week after her diagnosis.

Antibiotic names, doses and routes are not documented.
